title: BanFakeNews: A Dataset for Detecting Fake News in Bangla
abstract: Introduces the largest annotated Bangla dataset containing authentic and fabricated news spanning varied public sectors.
method: Dataset Curation, Baseline Naive Bayes, SVM, BiLSTM
key_findings: Establishes baseline performance benchmarks across standard models.
limitations: Contains geographic bias toward major national dailies.

title: BanglaBERT: Language Model Pre-training and Benchmarks for Low-Resource Language Understanding Evaluation in Bangla
abstract: A pretrained BERT model tailored for Bangla text processing across multiple downstream classification and generation benchmarks.
key_findings: Outperforms multilingual BERT on text classification benchmarks.
limitations: High computational training requirements; fine-tuning stability varies.

title: Fake News Detection in Bangla Social Media using Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores traditional machine learning approaches to identify fabricated news and rumor posts on Bangla social media platforms.
key_findings: SVM achieved 82 percent accuracy using linguistic features.
limitations: Limited to a small dataset of 2000 posts; lacks contextual semantics.

title: Deep Learning for Bangla Misinformation Detection on Online Portals
abstract: We present a deep learning architecture using bidirectional LSTM networks to detect fake news articles published in online newspapers.
key_findings: BiLSTM captured sequential patterns better than naive Bayes.
limitations: Fails on short clickbait headlines and non-standard colloquial dialects.

title: Cross-Domain Stance Detection in Bangla News Comments
abstract: Examines user stance towards news claims to cross-verify disputed statements and misinformation online.
key_findings: Stance correlation strongly aligns with rumor refutation signals.
limitations: Cross-domain generalization suffers without target-specific vocabulary.

title: Multimodal Misinformation Detection in Bengali Digital Media
abstract: Combines image analysis and Bangla text captions to verify social media claims containing misleading graphical content.
key_findings: Multimodal features outperform text-only models by 9 percent.
limitations: Small multimodal paired corpus limits generalizability.

title: Automated Fact-Checking Pipeline for Bengali News Verification
abstract: Proposes a semi-automated evidence retrieval and claim verification pipeline querying trusted news outlets.
key_findings: Automates initial evidence retrieval, cutting manual check latency.
limitations: Sensitive to query reformulation and missing indexed archives.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Rumor Propagation Analysis in Bangla Twitter
abstract: Analyzes the propagation topology of retweets and replies to detect fake news cascades without looking at text content.
key_findings: Cascade structure alone yields 78 percent rumor detection precision.
limitations: Requires dense propagation trees; cannot evaluate zero-engagement posts.

title: Linguistic Feature Engineering for Bangla Clickbait Classification
abstract: Extracts syntactic, sentiment, and punctuation markers to identify sensation-seeking clickbait headlines.
key_findings: Punctuation and punctuation density serve as high-yield signals.
limitations: Manual feature design degrades as headline styling practices evolve.

title: Transformer-based Hate Speech and Fake Information Detection in Bangla
abstract: Evaluates transformer architectures on abusive content and toxic false claims across youth gaming forums.
key_findings: Joint multi-task objectives boost performance on sparse labels.
limitations: Class imbalance among extreme toxicity subgroups degrades sensitivity.

title: Stylometric Analysis of Bangla Deceptive Texts
abstract: Quantifies author stylometry and vocabulary diversity to identify ghostwritten synthetic propaganda.
key_findings: Syntactic complexity is lower in artificially generated fake news.
limitations: Vulnerable to simple stylistic mimicry and professional paraphrasing.

title: Zero-Shot Rumor Classification in Low-Resource Indic Languages
abstract: Applies zero-shot cross-lingual inference from English source datasets to target Bangla social rumors.
key_findings: Cross-lingual transfer matches supervised baselines within 4 percent.
limitations: Susceptible to cultural idioms and local regional references.

title: Explainable AI for Bangla Fake News Using LIME and SHAP
abstract: Applies post-hoc interpretability frameworks to highlight lexical cues driving black-box transformer predictions.
key_findings: Word attribution reveals reliance on out-of-context emotive adjectives.
limitations: Feature attribution explanations can produce inconsistent local tokens.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Rumor Diffusion in Bangla Social Networks
abstract: Models the temporal velocity and retweeting lifespan of true vs false claims during election cycles.
key_findings: False rumors diffuse 3 times faster during the initial 2 hours.
limitations: High observation window required to estimate kernel parameters reliably.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Bangla Text Classifiers
abstract: Generates character-level typographical noise to test vulnerability of text classification models.
key_findings: Insertion of zero-width joiners reduces accuracy by over 35 percent.
limitations: Evaluated strictly on synthetic substitutions rather than natural human typos.

title: Bengali Claim Verification via Semantic Passage Retrieval
abstract: Leverages dense semantic retrieval to surface relevant evidence paragraphs against dubious user inputs.
key_findings: Dense semantic retrieval outperforms keyword BM25 on paraphrased queries.
limitations: Indexing latency scales poorly with corpus size.

title: Sentiment-Informed Misinformation Detection in Bengali Health Forums
abstract: Examines the interplay of alarmist emotional valence and false medical advice during epidemics.
key_findings: High negative emotional arousal correlates strongly with medical myths.
limitations: Domain-specific medical entity vocabulary is incomplete.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Emerging Rumors in Bangla Microblogs
abstract: Employs autoencoders on lexical embeddings to detect outlier discussion bursts indicative of rumors.
key_findings: Detects emerging rumor clusters without labeled training supervision.
limitations: Higher false positive rates on breaking authentic breaking news items.

title: Fine-Grained Misinformation Category Classification in Bangla
abstract: Categorizes misleading information into parody, imposter content, fabricated text, and manipulated media.
key_findings: Fine-grained categorization improves context-aware flagging accuracy.
limitations: Substantial annotator disagreement on satire vs malicious deception.

title: Network Community Detection for Disinformation Ring Tracking in Bangladesh
abstract: Analyzes coordinated inauthentic behavior via community detection algorithms on interaction graphs.
key_findings: Identified 14 primary sub-networks driving organized amplification.
limitations: Cannot identify isolated individual malicious actors operating independently.
